purpose: One bounded review of retained incident evidence and maintained GTK callback, worker, destroy and retirement boundaries. This is a risk disposition, not reproduction, repair, containment or release acceptance.

original_failure.signature: 17 completed tests, _gtk_css_rgba_value_get_rgba assertion 'rgba->class == &GTK_CSS_VALUE_RGBA' failed, then SIGSEGV
original_failure.earlier_observation: The same signature was retained before the Xv port work. The GTK settings suite does not load the Xv plugin.
original_failure.interpretation: Dots identify completed cases only. They do not establish which test, asynchronous callback, redraw or teardown executed the unsafe native operation. The core-dumped message does not provide a retained core artifact.

existing_observations_not_repeated.python_proxy_gc: Forced worker collection retired Python wrappers off-main. This alone did not identify native GTK finalization or the original crash.
existing_observations_not_repeated.native_lifetime: Original Ubuntu24 and corrected Ubuntu26 native GObject weak-finalizer observations recorded zero off-main finalizers. This does not prove all lifetime operations safe or causally explain the failure.
existing_observations_not_repeated.main_thread_test_retirement: Existing teardown destroys windows, waits for its owned worker, clears retained test cases, drains the main loop and collects cycles on the GTK thread. This is test retirement, not a demonstrated native-crash fix.
existing_observations_not_repeated.clean_runs: Prior ordinary and GDB runs, focused neighboring tests and subsequent CI were clean. A clean rerun is not causal repair evidence. GDB changes scheduling.
existing_observations_not_repeated.capture_controls: The existing one-execution Ubuntu24 GDB CI wrapper captures native and best-effort Python stacks, passes the original fatal signal and keeps failure status. Fatal and handled-signal controls were previously tested; none reproduce the original CSS failure.

maintained_boundaries_reviewed.observation: Worker closures retain core functions, immutable receipt inputs and a queue, rather than the SettingsWindow or widget callbacks. GTK status/preview changes occur in main-loop polling. Destroy closes the poller, increments its generation and removes its GLib source; late results remain queue data. No new off-main GTK operation was demonstrated.
maintained_boundaries_reviewed.limit: Reading this ownership structure and the earlier native observations cannot exclude an unknown native lifetime or scheduling fault.

maintained_boundaries_reviewed.observation: The accessible type is configured before the first entry instance, uses GTK-owned EntryAccessible lifetime and returns DEFUNCT after its widget is gone. Normal quit marks quitting before unsubscribing tray signals, deactivating its indicator and destroying the window. Modal confirmation uses a nested main loop; freshness is rechecked after confirmation before persistence. No retained incident stack ties these operations to the CSS failure.
maintained_boundaries_reviewed.limit: No claim that an unobserved reentrant callback, native accessible or CSS redraw path has been exhaustively proven safe.

maintained_boundaries_reviewed.observation: Existing tests distinguish late worker completion from publishing to destroyed widgets, preserve UI response assertions and retire test-owned references on the GTK thread. They do not reproduce the original CSS assertion.

areas: Native and best-effort Python fatal capture
Original-signal delivery and nonzero fatal result
maintained_boundaries_reviewed.observation: No retry, test-order change, fatal-warning suppression or successful-exit rewrite was introduced in this review. Controlled capture signals remain distinct from the original incident.

bounded_pass.reason_no_speculative_change: The original unsafe operation is not identified and no new reproducible own fault distinguished a proposed fix. Repeating clean suites or adding speculative teardown, scheduling, CSS or lifetime workarounds would not resolve that gap.
bounded_pass.tool_policy_block: No actual cybersecurity-filter or tool-policy block was observed in this pass.

disposition.issue_state: Keep #623 open as an intermittent, unreproduced GTK settings crash risk.
disposition.affected_scope: Observed in the optional GTK settings tests on hosted Ubuntu24; the original native failure is not attributed to a particular own or external component.
scope_not_inferred: Stock runtime stability established by clean CI
Failure of the stdlib CLI configuration editor
Failure of unrelated playback, native V4L2 or Xv execution
disposition.next_decisive_input: A recurrence with the existing native/Python capture and exact test name, or a discriminating reproducer that demonstrates an own unsafe callback, thread or lifetime operation.
disposition.continuation: Stop this bounded pass after retained evidence is exhausted. Continue other authorized release work with this unresolved risk explicit; do not wait indefinitely for a recurrence or label diagnostic capture as containment.
disposition.release_decision: This record neither grants nor blocks promotion by itself; apply the maintainer-authorized release criteria and preserve the unresolved GTK risk in the release assessment.
disposition.existing_unchanged_settings_scope: The already-recorded installed 31-case GTK, two private-bus tray cases and documented settings user flows remain scoped unchanged-component evidence; this review does not repeat or broaden them.
disposition.release_known_issue: An intermittent Ubuntu24 GTK settings CSS assertion/SIGSEGV remains unreproduced and unfixed. No failing native/Python stack or demonstrated own-code cause is available. Existing capture is diagnostic, not a repair, and no external GTK defect is established. No new unknown-reproduction gate is added; keep this optional-editor risk explicit under the authorized release criteria.
